run_rows.label: Rush EPA/play
run_rows.tooltip: Rushing efficiency, opponent-unadjusted (no rush-specific opp-adjusted variant exists yet -- only the overall off/def_epa_per_play_adj is opponent-adjusted)

run_rows.label: Rush success rate
run_rows.tooltip: Share of this offense's rush plays (downs 1-3) that stay on schedule by the standard down-and-distance success rule, vs the opposing defense's stuff rate (runs stopped at/behind the line) -- the closest real pairing, not a matched metric

run_rows.label: Chunk-run rate (10+)
run_rows.tooltip: Share of rush plays gaining 10+ yards (the standard explosive-run threshold): this offense's own rate vs the opposing defense's chunk-runs-allowed rate

run_rows.label: Yards after contact/carry
run_rows.tooltip: Team yards after contact per carry. No opposing-defense counterpart is shown: the run-defense metric that used to sit here (average depth of tackle) has no equivalent in the current data, and the alternatives measured too unreliable to rank

run_rows.label: OL continuity index
run_rows.tooltip: Share of this offensive line's (C/G/T) snaps played by linemen who also logged OL snaps for this team last season, vs the opposing front seven's (DI/ED/LB) own returning-snap share -- continuity/disposition, not a quality judgment

run_rows.label: Back rushing yards
run_rows.tooltip: Rushing yards a game by running backs, gained against allowed. Position comes from the rusher's own row, so a quarterback's runs are counted separately rather than inflating this.

run_rows.label: Rushing TDs a game
run_rows.tooltip: Rushing touchdowns a game, scored against allowed. The half of the run game a lineup actually turns on.

run_rows.label: Red-zone rush TD rate
run_rows.tooltip: Share of carries inside the 20 that reach the end zone, scored against allowed. Needs 15 red-zone carries, so it arrives around week five rather than being guessed before then.

run_rows.label: Yards per carry
run_rows.tooltip: Rushing yards per carry, gained against allowed. Sacks, kneels and team rushes are excluded -- a sack is a rush attempt in most sources, and counting it here would grade the pass protection instead of the running game. Split-half repeatability +0.387 offense, +0.339 defense.

run_rows.label: Run first-down rate
run_rows.tooltip: Share of carries that move the chains, gained against allowed. Split-half repeatability +0.444 offense, +0.374 defense. Carries where the feed published no down and distance are left out of both halves -- CFBD omits them on 12.6% of carries and the omission is team-shaped, so counting them as failures ranked how completely each team's feed was published.

run_rows.label: O-Line push vs Front
run_rows.tooltip: Offense's line-yards (CFBD advanced, O-line push metric) vs the opposing defense's stuff rate (how often it stops runs at/behind the line) -- the closest real trench pairing available, not a matched metric

run_rows.label: Power success vs Havoc
run_rows.tooltip: Offense's power-success rate (3rd/4th-and-short conversion) vs the opposing front seven's havoc rate

pass_rows.label: Pass EPA/dropback
pass_rows.tooltip: Passing efficiency, opponent-unadjusted (no pass-specific opp-adjusted variant exists yet)

pass_rows.label: Hurry rate
pass_rows.tooltip: Quarterback hurries per dropback: this offense's hurries ALLOWED against the opposing defense's hurries GENERATED, both from the official box score. Each rank describes its own team -- a high offensive rank is a line that keeps its quarterback clean, a high defensive rank is a front that gets home.

pass_rows.label: QB rushing yards
pass_rows.tooltip: Rushing yards a game by quarterbacks, gained against allowed. Position comes from the rusher's own row. A defense that has not faced a running quarterback will read well here for a reason that is about its schedule.

pass_rows.label: Passing TDs a game
pass_rows.tooltip: Passing touchdowns a game, thrown against allowed.

pass_rows.label: Red-zone pass TD rate
pass_rows.tooltip: Share of attempts inside the 20 that reach the end zone, thrown against allowed. Needs 15 red-zone attempts, so it arrives around week five rather than being guessed before then.

pass_rows.label: Sack rate
pass_rows.tooltip: Offense's sacks-taken rate (lower is better for offense) vs the opposing defense's sacks-generated rate

pass_rows.label: Turnover rate
pass_rows.tooltip: All turnovers (not pass-exclusive) -- offense's giveaway rate vs the opposing defense's takeaway rate

pass_rows.label: Third-down rate
pass_rows.tooltip: Share of third downs converted, for and against, pooled across the season from the official box score rather than averaged per game -- a 1-for-2 game must not weigh the same as a 9-for-18 one. An unpublished box-score category is skipped, never counted as a zero.

perim_rows.label: Depth of target
perim_rows.tooltip: Average air yards per attempt -- how far downfield this offense throws, against how far downfield this defense allows throws. Throwaways and spikes are excluded: both are attempts in a box score and neither is a throw at anybody. DEPTH IS A STYLE, NOT A GRADE -- a checkdown offense is not a worse one.

perim_rows.label: Catch rate
perim_rows.tooltip: Completions per attempt, for and against. Read it beside depth of target: an offense throwing 12 yards downfield completes fewer by role, not by accuracy.

perim_rows.label: Yards after catch
perim_rows.tooltip: Yards gained after the catch, per reception, for and against. Needs 30 receptions carrying the figure -- yards after catch is recorded on completions only and on roughly half of those, so this arrives later in a season than the rows above it.

perim_rows.label: Explosive catch rate
perim_rows.tooltip: Share of dropbacks producing a 15-yard-or-longer gain through the air, for and against. THE DENOMINATOR IS ATTEMPTS, not catches -- an incompletion cannot be explosive and sits in the denominator, so this is explosive plays per dropback. Split-half +0.407 offense, +0.308 defense.

perim_rows.label: Deep target rate
perim_rows.tooltip: Share of throws travelling 20 or more yards in the air, for and against. A STYLE, NOT A GRADE -- read it beside depth of target, not as better or worse. The denominator counts only attempts that carry a recorded depth: roughly 3% do not, and counting those as not-deep would understate each offense by however much of its data is missing.

drive_rows.label: Yards per drive
drive_rows.tooltip: Yards gained per possession, for and against. The most repeatable twin on the whole tab: split-half +0.627 offense, +0.436 defense.

drive_rows.label: Points per drive
drive_rows.tooltip: Points scored per possession, for and against. Points come from the offense's own score columns, never from the drive's `scoring` flag -- that flag is true when EITHER side scored, and a pick-six carries it with the offense scoring nothing.

drive_rows.label: TD per drive
drive_rows.tooltip: Share of possessions ending in a touchdown, for and against. Six points, so a two-point conversion counts with it and a field goal does not.

drive_rows.label: Trips inside the 40
drive_rows.tooltip: Scoring chances a game -- possessions advancing to the opponent's 40 -- created against allowed. This is the denominator under every red-zone row on the tab: a red-zone rate means something different on three chances a game than on one. Built from the drive table, which is why it differs slightly from the play-derived scoring-opportunity count on the same page.

drive_rows.label: Three-and-out rate
drive_rows.tooltip: Share of possessions ending in three plays or fewer with no points, for and against. The offense's rank is better when the rate is lower; the defense's is better when it is higher, and each percentile describes its own team.

drive_rows.label: Drive start (yds to goal)
drive_rows.tooltip: Average yards still to travel at the start of a possession, taken against conceded. IT COUNTS DOWN: 25 is a short field and 80 is a long one, so a SMALLER number is better for an offense. The percentile already reads the right way round; the raw number does not.

drive_rows.label: Team penalty yards a game
drive_rows.tooltip: Penalty yards a game: this team's own, against what its opponents have been charged. A WHOLE-TEAM figure, not an offensive one -- the box score counts a team's penalties without splitting them by unit. And a defense does not force a penalty: its column is only what the other side was charged while playing it.

situational_rows.label: 3rd down success rate
situational_rows.tooltip: Real weighted average of the short/med/long 3rd-down success-rate cells, weighted by this team's own 3rd-down distance profile

situational_rows.label: Neutral-script pass rate
situational_rows.tooltip: This team's real pass rate when the score is within one score (team_game_script, garbage-time excluded) -- game-script identity, not compared against the opponent (no real defense-side equivalent exists)

situational_rows.label: 2nd-and-long EPA
situational_rows.tooltip: Real offensive EPA on 2nd-and-long for the offense side; defense's own 2nd-and-long EPA allowed shown for context, not a matched opponent-facing pair

redzone_rows.label: Red zone EPA
redzone_rows.tooltip: Offense's EPA/play once inside the opponent's 20 -- no defense-allowed red-zone data exists in this pipeline yet, so this is offense identity, not a collision

redzone_rows.label: Red zone TD rate
redzone_rows.tooltip: Share of red-zone trips ending in a touchdown

redzone_rows.label: Points per opportunity
redzone_rows.tooltip: Bill Connelly's standard metric: points scored per real scoring opportunity (drive reaching the opponent's 40)

identity_levers.tooltip: Share of offensive plays that are a pass
Seconds per play, lower = faster tempo
Pass rate over expected -- our own down/distance/field/score model (specs/proe-xpass-model.md); positive = passes more than situation suggests
Offense's own real plays-per-game (tempo) vs the defense's own real plays-faced-per-game -- each team's real number, not a matched opponent pair
Defense's real blitz rate -- a tendency, not a quality judgment
Offense's real neutral-script pass rate (team_game_script, garbage-time excluded) -- ball-control identity; no real defense-side equivalent
Offense's real pass rate when leading (team_game_script, garbage-time excluded) -- ball-control identity; no real defense-side equivalent
Offense's real play-action rate (charting) vs the defense's own real coverage yards allowed per snap (team_percentiles) -- a real, asymmetric pairing, not a matched opponent stat
